column1: # The TF2 Stage 0 seams: what a mod hooks, who may own it, where the core asks it, and the facts that prove both arms. SeamsLedgerTests keeps every row true (types, dispatch symbols, fact methods).

# Chain participants (owner_rule chain, set-unique-id, single-per-key sources): SideServices lets ONE class per side claim a contract through As = [typeof(IX)] (a second claimant is a startup error, SideServices.Register), so participants from several mods use the plain [SideService(Side.X)] mark, which ServiceContainer.ResolveAll finds by type. Only the owner_rule single seams take As = [typeof(IX)].
# interface: a core type (Namespace.Type), a member of one (Namespace.Type.Member), or non-type:<name>. dispatch and facts: path::Type.Member and TestClass.Method, several separated by ", ".

column7: notes
Resolved once per side after the mods register and frozen; two hooks are a startup error naming both types and assemblies. No hook: MovementRules.Stock.

Append-only: core rows first, then sources by assembly name (HookOrder.Sorted). A duplicate or empty name is refused with a warning; the first owner keeps the index. The index is the wire format (WeaponTypeId).
As IWeaponTypeSource. WireIndex counts from 1 (CAmmoDef).

Sources are a chain sorted by assembly name; each IWeaponBehaviour key has one owner (the first source to claim it; a later claim is refused with a warning). WeaponType.Behaviour picks the key; an unresolved key runs stock with one warning.

Resolved lazily after the mods register, then frozen; two policies throw naming both. Playing teams only: team 1 and out-of-range numbers go to Observers. No policy accepts any real team (a divergence from stock HL2DM).
IHooks in HookOrder, ties refused; the first non-None answer wins; a throw is logged and falls through. The active mode's Spawns is asked first; None falls back to the core walk.
IHooks in HookOrder, ties refused, asked before every stock verb; the first true owns the word; a throw is logged and the next hook is asked.
Every registered mode is selectable by Id; a duplicate Id is a startup refusal naming both. NullMode ("null") is appended last, so a mod's "null" wins.
IHooks in HookOrder, ties refused; the first non-empty id wins; a throw is skipped; the core's "null" answers last. An unknown id logs and leaves the core rules running.
The active mode's IRoundFlow (required). NullMode.Rounds is the rules object; reference guards prevent a double call. Intermission stays core.
The active mode's ISpawnSelector, asked before the registered chain; None or a throw falls through.
The active mode's IRespawnPolicy, read on every call; null means the core 3 s wait and a plain yes.
The active mode's IScoring; null means the core scoreboard only. A shared scoring object is reset once per switch (by reference).
The active mode's IModeSetup, after the flush and before the warmup; null prepares nothing; a throw is logged and the round still starts.
A virtual (the plan's IRoundResettable was never made an interface): each class opts in by overriding; the default is a no-op. Reset in place on a switch, not CleanUpMap (a divergence row).
IHooks in HookOrder, ties refused; the first answer other than UseStockRule wins; a throw declines. Asked only where the core deferred: spawn protection and friendly fire cannot be opened.
IHooks in HookOrder, ties refused; the last provider to name a column (weapons, ammo) wins it; a throw is skipped.
Every source asked; components ordered by the component's assembly name, then IPlayerComponent.Order; a throw is skipped. Get<T>(player) finds a component across mods.
Pre-dates Stage 0 (plan_descent_death). IHooks.Each in HookOrder, ties refused; every hook runs, a throw is logged.
Pre-dates Stage 0. A veto chain: gates asked in HookOrder until one refuses; any refusal vetoes; a throw allows.

Every layer in the side's container plus the core's Hl2PostureLayer (LayerOrder 1000), ordered by LayerOrder, ties refused (StageCollisionException); the first true wins. Both sides compose identically (prediction). A layer is one object per side: it reads the player from AnimStateContext.Target.

Additive: the core's fixed list first, then the container's handlers; a name already handled keeps its handler and the mod's is refused with a warning. Managed handlers are asked before the native registrations.

Every UiScreen in the mods.yaml assemblies.client_ui assemblies, built through the container (not a [SideService]); core screens keep their order, mod screens follow per layer by UiScreen.Order. The no-owner fact's control arm: no mod list, no mod screen. Loaded in the UI's collectible context (cs_ui_reload).

mods.yaml localisation: [...]. First file wins: the mod's disk language file, each listed file in order (IEngineFiles, VPK-capable), the core #SS_UI_ strings, then the engine's Localise. The no-owner fact's control arm: an unlisted file does not resolve.
